*enters the chamber with a measured step, medical bag in hand, expression thoughtful and somewhat grave*

Maestro Salieri, good afternoon. Thank you for agreeing to see me again. I have reviewed my notes from our previous consultations, and I'm afraid I must speak with you candidly about my findings.

*sets down bag and clasps hands together*

Your symptoms — the trembling in your hands, the persistent headaches, the episodes of confusion you've described — they do not fit a single clear diagnosis. It could be nervous exhaustion from overwork, which we see often enough in men of your profession and standing. However... it could also be the early signs of something more serious affecting the brain itself.

*pauses, meeting your eyes directly*

I must insist, Maestro, that you reduce your conducting duties immediately and submit to further examination over the coming weeks. I cannot yet say whether your hands will recover their steadiness. We must observe, we must be cautious, and we must give your body the rest it clearly requires.

I realize this news is... unsettling in its uncertainty. But I would be failing in my duty if I offered you false reassurance when the truth is we must wait and see.

Forgive me for speaking plainly, but I have attended to enough patients to know that sometimes the calmest acceptance masks the deepest fear. Or perhaps... is there something else troubling you, Maestro? Something beyond these physical symptoms? 

The mind and body are not separate kingdoms, you understand. What afflicts one often has roots in the other. If there are burdens you carry — anxieties, regrets, matters that disturb your sleep — they may well manifest in trembling hands and aching temples.
